architecture.title: Two Sparks, one cluster — management network for control, QSFP link for data
architecture.caption: Your laptop drives both Sparks over SSH on the management network (Ethernet enP7s7, Wi-Fi or Tailscale). One QSFP cable joins the ConnectX-7 chips directly; each physical port shows up as two logical interfaces, each on its own /24 subnet (192.168.100.x and 192.168.101.x in the playbook). mpirun starts on Spark A and SSHes to Spark B; NCCL sends the bulk data over the RoCE devices on the cable.

sequence.title: Lab 02-3 — one NCCL all-gather test across two Sparks
sequence.caption: The lab checks the build on both Sparks, reads both management IPs, and runs the playbook's mpirun command on Spark A. mpirun starts rank 1 on Spark B over SSH; the ranks exchange 16 GB over the QSFP link. The lab parses the nccl-tests table and compares '# Avg bus bandwidth' with the 21.875 GB/s pass mark from NVIDIA's cluster script. In DRY mode the table is an EXAMPLE; the parser is also tested on NVIDIA's real RDMA sample.

charts.title: Bandwidth at each layer, in GB/s
charts.caption: Memory: DGX Spark spec. Line rate: 200 ÷ 8. RDMA: the playbook's ib_write_bw sample, 92.57 + 97.28 = 189.85 Gb/s ÷ 8 (re-computed by lab 03). Pass marks: MIN_NCCL_TEST_BW and MIN_NCCL_TEST_BW_RING in NVIDIA's spark_cluster_setup.py. The cable is about 12× slower than memory, so only activations cross it.

charts.title: Per-token time, one Spark vs TP=2 (α = 30 µs assumed)
charts.caption: From lab 04 (arithmetic, not a measurement): NVFP4-sized weights read at 273 GB/s, plus 2 × layers all-reduces at an ASSUMED 30 µs latency and 21.875 GB/s busbw. At 100 µs gpt-oss-120b becomes slower on two Sparks (0.84×). Module 05 measures real numbers.
